notes: Made.com UK (Next-operated storefront). Found a genuine sitewide New Arrivals PLP at https://www.made.com/shop/f/feat-newin - page title 'Buy New In Online', SSR JSON search.totalResults:122, feat facet correctly resolves (unlike the invalid feat-bestseller/feat-popular probes tried for the Bestsellers file, which fell back to the unfiltered generic template). QTY INDEPENDENTLY VERIFIED BY EXHAUSTION, same method used in the prior Home-Decor pass for this company: extracted itemNumber (structured product-ID field) from the base page (84 unique IDs, matching the site's known 7x12 SSR prefetch chunking) then paged ?p=8..12 to cover the remainder; unique itemNumber count converged to exactly 122 with zero new IDs beyond p=8-11 and zero items on p=12, matching search.totalResults exactly on every page fetched. Every category page also exposes a per-category 'New In' filter (e.g. /shop/lighting/ceiling-lights/f/feat-newin, 13 items) alongside Colour/Material/Sale filters in the same generic facet block - this is an arbitrary cross-category filter applied uniformly to every listing, not a site-curated 'New Arrivals > Department New Arrivals' navigation tree (contrast with the site's genuine Lighting > Room sub-structure documented in the prior pass, which had its own indexed canonical nav entries). Per brief guidance on arbitrary filter pages, these per-category New In facets were excluded as child rows; only the single sitewide New In listing is reported. Also checked and excluded: /new-in and /shop/new-in resolve to the site's generic empty catch-all template (totalResults:0, same auto-title pattern confirmed via a nonsense-slug control request), so no separate curated 'New Arrivals' landing page exists distinct from the feat-newin facet. Sitemap (12,150 category + 47 collection URLs) has no dedicated New Arrivals URL indexed (feat-newin is robots-disallowed from the sitemap generator, consistent with it being a facet rather than a crawlable category), but the page itself is live and fully functional when fetched directly.
